sections.facts: The appellant landlord applied to the Rent Controller on December 1, 1956, under section 13(3) of the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act for the eviction of the respondent tenant to remedy certain defects in the leased building. On April 11, 1957, the Municipal Committee issued an amended notice requiring only that the cracked pillar be reinforced so as to make it a solid block, and the respondent carried out the repairs. On June 8, 1957, the Executive Engineer inspected again pursuant to the order of the Rent Controller and was satisfied that the pillar had been satisfactorily repaired. The Rent Controller held that the case fell within section 13(3)(a) of the Act and ordered eviction. On appeal, the District Judge, taking note of the state of repairs, allowed the appeal. In revision under section 15(5) of the Act, the High Court Judge held that the High Court's revisionary powers were similar to those under section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code and involved no question of jurisdiction, but affirmed the decision after considering the evidence.
sections.statute: Section 13(3), Section 13(3)(a), and Section 15(5) of the Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act; Section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code.
sections.analysis: The powers of the High Court under section 15(5) of the Act are manifestly wider than those under section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code and are not confined to questions of jurisdiction. Furthermore, under section 13(3)(a), the requirement of vacant possession by the landlord can only be for the purpose of carrying out such fundamental and extensive repairs as cannot be carried out without evicting the tenant, and not for minor repairs.
sections.judgement: Held, it was open to the District Judge to consider the subsequent events up to the time when eviction was ordered by the Controller in view of the scheme and purpose of the legislation.
